questions.q: What problem does a single-stage Dockerfile create when a package needs to compile native code during installation?
options: The build fails every time
The compiler toolchain used only during install gets baked permanently into the final image
Python cannot be installed at all
The image becomes impossible to push to a registry
questions.explain: A single-stage build carries the full compiler toolchain forward into the final image even though it's never used again after `pip install` finishes.

questions.q: What does `FROM python:3.12 AS builder` do?
options: Deletes the python:3.12 base image
Automatically installs build-essential
Makes this the final, published image
Names this stage "builder" so a later stage can reference it with COPY --from=builder
questions.explain: The AS clause names a build stage, which a later stage can then selectively copy files from.

questions.q: In a two-stage Dockerfile, what actually ends up in the final runtime image?
options: Only the files a later stage explicitly copies with COPY --from=<stage name>
Every file from every stage, merged together
Only the files from the very first stage
Nothing — multi-stage builds produce an empty image
questions.explain: Everything else in an earlier stage — compilers, package caches, intermediate files — is discarded once the build finishes, unless explicitly copied forward.

questions.q: Why does a smaller final image matter beyond just disk space, per this lesson?
options: Smaller images cannot run on GPUs
It has no practical effect on anything
A smaller image pulls faster, which matters directly for autoscaling startup time (Chapter 4)
Smaller images automatically fix security vulnerabilities
questions.explain: Faster pulls mean faster container startup — relevant once autoscaling needs new instances to come online quickly.

questions.q: In the example multi-stage Dockerfile, which base image is used for the final runtime stage?
options: python:3.12-slim
python:3.12 (same as the builder stage)
ubuntu:latest
An empty, scratch image
questions.explain: The runtime stage uses the slimmer python:3.12-slim base, since it no longer needs the compiler toolchain the builder stage required.
